ai_overview.lead: A prenuptial agreement (known in Australia as a Binding Financial Agreement or BFA) is a written contract made before marriage or a de facto relationship that sets out how property, debts, superannuation, and spousal maintenance will be handled if the relationship ends.
sections: What a Prenup Covers in Australia (pre-existing assets, business interests, inheritances, superannuation, debts)
What a Prenup Cannot Cover (parenting, child support, lifestyle clauses)
Legal Requirements for a Valid Australian BFA (independent legal advice, signed certificates, full disclosure, no duress) citing Family Law Act 1975
Why Couples Get Them (blended families, unequal wealth, reducing conflict)
